name: Usability Script
description_text:
Usability Script ( for your Final Project )
Your usability script is designed to uncover qualitative and quantitive data to back up your presumptions found in your Client Heuristics Doc. Make sure your script and questions will uncover if those issues are incurred by your usability test respondents.

Make sure your usability script is walking through at least two of the top tasks outlined in your persona. The script should take around 30 minutes to complete for a usability subject. You will want to ask as many of the types of questions outlined from our lecture that you feel are appropriate for that task to narrow down what you see are issues with the site.

Prepare your interview script to include the following:

Interview questions that help refine or verify your assumptions for your persona. 

Feedback to confirm your findings in your Heuristics Document. Try to use these methods to uncover user intent:

Track accuracy of user expectations: For example, "From this page, how would you..."  or "From this screen, what do you think this service/application is for?"

Usability of prototype: For example, "From a star rating of 1-5, 5 being best, how easy  would you rate this experience" 

Value and brand halo of experience: For example, "From a star rating of 1-5, 5 being best, how likely would you be to using this tool/service?"

3) Interview TWO respondents for each member of your team:

Each team member must interview two people, with each interview lasting about 20 minutes

You will need to shadow at least 2 interviews of somebody else on your team, taking notes on their behalf

4) Track results:

Record in a central location a spreadsheet for your findings. Each column should be a question and each user's response should be a row. Sample Spreadsheets here:

Tanooki-Research-data.xlsx

World Vision Interview Notes.xls

Interview Responses.xlsx

 

Your questions should try to cover the following topics:

Does it have the appropriate functionality?

Is the branding providing a positive response?

Does the content support the user goals?

Are the actions the user looking to do findable, intuitive and provide good usability? 

Example question types are:

Needs from the software/online service

Value proposition of the software/online service

Findability of elements

Expectations set by navigation elements

Gap between expectations and reality

Comprehension of text

Intention to perform a given action

Ease of performing a task

Friction points in performing a task

Improvements they feel should be made

Motivators/facilitators to continuing

Inhibitors/barriers to continuing

Preference between options

The aesthetic appeal

The trust in the system

The perceived speed, responsiveness

Memory for a previous stimulus

Learning along the flow

lecture_alignment.definition: The structural design of information environments to support usability and findability through organized, labeled, and navigable content systems.
Systematic investigation of users, their needs, behaviors, and contexts to inform design decisions through qualitative and quantitative methods.
Evaluative research method where representative users attempt tasks with a product to identify usability issues and measure performance.
The strategic development of visual and verbal identity systems that communicate an organization's values, personality, and positioning.
Creating interactive representations of designs at varying levels of fidelity to test concepts, gather feedback, and communicate ideas.
